paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Real faith does something. James asks, "What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith, but has no deeds?" (James 2:14). Then he says, "faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead" (James 2:17). Think of a cookie box with a beautiful label and nothing inside. Looks great on the shelf, feeds NOBODY.

Now, James isn't saying your deeds earn your way in. He's saying faith and action belong together, like the body and the spirit (James 2:26). Abraham is the proof, because his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did (James 2:22). And Rahab welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route (James 2:25). Two very different people, one very same pattern: they trusted God, and it showed up in their hands.

So what does that mean for you today? Believing the right things is a good start, but James reminds us that even the demons believe that God is one (James 2:19). Faith that is alive shows up when someone is hungry, cold or in need, and it doesn't just say "stay warm" and walk off. I'm the guy who spent years in a junk drawer saying I believed in the oven, and the oven didn't care until I got out and baked! So go and be the baker whose faith has flour on its hands.
